name: programming-ime-vscode-bridge
description: Seven-language local suggestions, per-hunk reviewed F1 AI edits and BYOK AI for Programming IME. The editor-side bridge of the system IME design; not a TSF input method.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In an untrusted workspace AI is disabled; local candidates keep working.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Whole-file F1 edits need a real file or untitled buffer.

programmingIme.enabled.description: Enable candidates and the F1 binding. While off, F1 keeps opening the Command Palette.

programmingIme.uiLocale.description: UI language of Programming IME. Independent of the Windows input language and of the programming profile.

programmingIme.suggestMode.description: auto: inline suggestions while typing. explicit: only when you press Ctrl+Alt+Space.

programmingIme.pinnedCandidates.description: Candidate ids that always rank first.

programmingIme.f1Binding.description: Key that opens the F1 AI edit panel when Programming IME is enabled. Use shift+f1 or none to keep F1 for the Command Palette.

programmingIme.f1ExcludedLanguages.description: Language ids in which the F1 binding is never taken over.

enumDescriptions: F1 opens on the Annotate tab. With no selection it finds the declaration (function, class, ...) around the cursor and adds comments to it; with a selection it comments exactly the selected lines. Only comment lines are added, your code is never rewritten.
F1 behaves as before: it opens on the Whole file tab and Generate asks for a whole-file change and an insertion. The Annotate tab stays available but idle.
programmingIme.f1Mode.description: What F1 does. annotate: add comments to the scope under the cursor, or to the selection. edit: the whole-file change and insert-at-cursor proposals of earlier versions.

programmingIme.f1AnnotateOnOpen.description: With programmingIme.f1Mode=annotate: start the annotation as soon as F1 opens (one request to your AI provider, after you have authorised the transfer). Off: F1 only shows the scope and waits for Generate. Needs AI on and a configured provider; the Comments / Cypher graph choice comes from autoComment / graphComment.

programmingIme.f2Binding.description: Key that copies a 5W1H prompt for the selected text or code when Programming IME is enabled. F2 normally renames a symbol: this binding only applies while the editor has a non-empty selection, so F2 without a selection still renames. Use shift+f2 or none to keep F2 for Rename in every case.

programmingIme.f2ExcludedLanguages.description: Language ids in which the F2 binding is never taken over (F2 keeps renaming, also with a selection).

programmingIme.engine.markdownDescription: Who runs the editor logic. `js`: the built-in JavaScript engine (a configured core only speeds up local candidates). `rust`: the Rust core in `programmingIme.coreExecutable` is REQUIRED; if it is missing or stops, the IME features are turned off and a message says why (there is no silent fallback; typing in VS Code is never affected). Reload the window after changing it.

programmingIme.coreExecutable.description: Absolute path of a trusted, locally built pime-core executable (protocol 0.2 or 0.3; the Rust engine needs 0.3). Empty uses the built-in JavaScript engine.

programmingIme.aiEnabled.description: Master switch. While off, no AI request is ever sent, whatever else is configured.

programmingIme.realtimeAI.description: Send authorised nearby code to the realtime provider for suggestions. Needs aiEnabled and a workspace authorisation.

programmingIme.autoComment.description: Attach very detailed, beginner-level comments to code you insert from the candidate list. Uses your own AI provider, which receives the WHOLE current file (with your authorisation) so the comments are accurate. Does nothing while AI is off or not configured. The AI may only add comments: if it changes any code the comments are discarded.

programmingIme.graphComment.description: Also attach a Cypher comment block (nodes and edges) that relates the inserted code to other symbols in the current file and, with graphCommentScope=directory, to the names of symbols in the files of the same folder. Off by default because it sends additional (name-only) workspace information to your AI provider.

programmingIme.graphCommentScope.description: file: relate the code only to symbols of the current file. directory: also to symbol NAMES (never code) found in other files of the same folder.

programmingIme.providers.description: Provider profiles: id -> {api, endpoint}. api is openai-responses, openai-chat or anthropic-messages. Optional per provider: apiVersion (anthropic-messages only, default 2026-10-21) and maxTokensParam (openai-chat only: max_tokens, or max_completion_tokens for OpenAI reasoning models). Keys are stored in SecretStorage, never here.

programmingIme.scenarios.description: Independent settings for realtime, f1Full and f1Insert: provider, model, effort, effortCapability, maxOutputTokens, timeoutMs.

programmingIme.budget.description: {maxRequests, maxTokens, pricePer1kTokens}. 0 means unlimited. When reached, AI stops; local input is unaffected.
